title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
abstract: arXiv:2611.17811v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper's presentation and content related to its core idea. translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被审稿人用来在审稿过程中指出论文的弱点，其输出往往会塑造人类最终提交的审稿意见。先前的研究探讨了LLM审稿与人类审稿的一致性，但对于这些模型实际批评论文的哪些部分，我们知之甚少。在本工作中，我们研究了来自ACL、EMNLP、COLM和ICLR的2000篇论文，发现最新的GPT和Claude模型约50%或更多的审稿弱点来自论文的附录。这一行为在使用LLM审稿的API、编程代理和网络访问三种方式中均普遍存在。相比之下，我们发现人类只有8.4%的弱点来自附录，且这些弱点主要围绕论文的表述方式以及与其核心思想相关的内容。与此同时，LLM从附录深处提取的弱点则涉及与论文核心贡献无关的细粒度技术细节。
tldr: 研究发现GPT和Claude等大语言模型在审稿时约50%以上的批评意见来自论文附录，而人类仅有8.4%，且AI的批评多集中于与核心贡献无关的细节，揭示了AI审稿存在系统性偏向附录的偏差。
en_tdlr: LLM-based reviewers such as GPT and Claude draw 50% or more of their review criticisms from a paper's appendix—compared to only 8.4% by humans—revealing a systematic bias of AI reviews toward appendix content.
